runtime_note: Predicate logic is fully static and exhaustively solved by z3 over the complete enum domain {posix, nt}: nt->True, posix->False. But os.name is a runtime OS probe set by the CPython interpreter at startup from the live platform kernel; it is NOT reachable from any CLI arg, YAML key, env var, or Tensile public input. A caller cannot drive this branch without changing the host OS (or monkeypatching os.name, as Tensile/Tests/unit/test_ClientExecutable.py does). Hence classification=runtime-dependent: witnesses are real z3 models but the taken branch is environment-determined. On the char-test host (posix, verified os.name==posix in tl-char) the Windows branch is unreachable. Sibling guard line 86 (_windowsWithExtensions, branch cc98dba0) is the same probe, classified identically.
solver_assumptions: os.name treated as a free enum variable over seeded domain {posix, nt}. In production os.name is fixed per host and not an input; posix is the only reachable branch on the char-test host without monkeypatch. java/Jython excluded since this is CPython.
